name: Expo (React Native) + FastAPI + PostgreSQL, offline/sync
description: Buaflow's mobile golden stack: an Expo (React Native + TypeScript) client with an offline-first local store (SQLite on native, localStorage on the web export — see docs/sync-contract.md for why), synced against a FastAPI + PostgreSQL backend through a pull/push sync API with last-write-wins conflict resolution. Materially different from the two web golden stacks: the client persists data locally BEFORE any network round trip, and the API contract is a sync protocol (cursor-based pull, batched push with per-change outcomes), not plain CRUD.

inputs.name: projectName
inputs.description: Package name used for the mobile app's and backend's manifests of the generated app.

inputs.name: includeAuth
inputs.description: Scaffold a starter bearer-token auth module (login returns a signed token used as an Authorization header, since a native mobile client has no browser cookie jar).

inputs.name: orm
inputs.description: ORM used by the backend to talk to PostgreSQL.

inputs.name: localStore
inputs.description: On-device persistence used by the native (iOS/Android) build. The web export target always uses localStorage instead — see docs/sync-contract.md; this is a platform split, not a generator input choice.

setup.description: Expo's own generator creates the React Native + TypeScript client, unpinned so the SDK version is whatever Expo currently ships.

setup.command: cd mobile && npx expo install expo-sqlite expo-secure-store react-native-web react-dom @expo/metro-runtime
setup.description: `expo install` rather than `npm install` on purpose: it resolves each package to the version matching the installed SDK, which npm cannot do.

setup.command: python -m venv backend/.venv && backend/.venv/bin/pip install fastapi uvicorn[standard] sqlalchemy alembic psycopg[binary] pydantic-settings bcrypt
setup.description: The sync backend. Bearer-token auth needs a password hasher, since a native client has no browser cookie jar to fall back on.
Server-side migration history; the client keeps its own local store separately, documented in the sync contract.

requiredArtifacts.description: SQLAlchemy models — updated_at/deleted_at are the sync cursor, the conflict-resolution version and the tombstone the protocol needs.
The sync contract itself: cursor-based pull and batched push with per-change last-write-wins outcomes.
The pure, storage-agnostic client-side sync engine — exhaustively unit-testable without a device or a network.
The documented offline/sync contract, including why the web export uses a different local store than the native build.
Multi-stage production build (mobile web export -> Python runtime); the native iOS/Android build is a separate, non-containerized artifact.

verification.command: cd backend && mypy app && cd ../mobile && npm run typecheck
verification.description: Backend strict mypy and the mobile TypeScript app both compile with no errors.

verification.command: cd backend && pytest && cd ../mobile && npm test && cd ../tests/e2e && npm test
verification.description: Backend sync integration suite, the mobile app's pure sync-engine unit suite, and the e2e suite (including a genuine offline/online round trip) all pass.
Production multi-stage build succeeds, proving the web deployment-package control.

operationalEvidence.evidence: Alembic migrations under backend/alembic/versions/ give a repeatable, versioned server-side persistence lifecycle; the client's own local persistence is documented and tested separately in docs/sync-contract.md.
Alembic supports a real downgrade() natively; the migration ships forward and backward paths together, rehearsed end to end — same mechanism as react-fastapi-postgres.

The multi-stage Dockerfile builds a pinned, reproducible production image serving the mobile web export directly from FastAPI; a debug Android APK built via expo prebuild and Gradle in CI proves the native distribution channel compiles and links.
